rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis proposes vapor-coating W particles with Cu before sintering, whereas the paper uses liquid-metal dealloying of a WTaVTi RHEA precursor in molten Cu to create a bicontinuous RHEA–Cu composite. These are fundamentally different kinds of interventions.
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis specifies spark plasma sintering and fusion-reactor irradiation conditions, while the paper uses vacuum-sealed silica ampoule immersion in molten Cu at 1200 °C for 96 h, thermal conductivity measurement up to 800 °C, and 25 keV He+ irradiation. The conditions are entirely different.
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis invokes enhanced wettability and diffusion from a pre-applied Cu coating to minimize voids, whereas the paper's mechanism relies on selective Ti dissolution from interdendritic channels, W-rich interlayer passivation, and aligned Cu channels for conductivity. These are different classes of mechanism.
rationale.outcome_agreement: The hypothesis predicts improved thermal conductivity and mechanical durability relative to uncoated W–Cu composites, while the paper predicts and measures thermal conductivity surpassing pure W at high temperature and reduced He-induced swelling relative to pure W. The predicted properties and comparisons differ.
